================================================================================================================
F. METHOD, AND WHAT EACH SIGNAL IS ACTUALLY WORTH
================================================================================================================

Signal 1 -- FILE/TEST COUNTS. Exact. Read straight out of the source tree with a
  recursive walk of engine/tests/test_modules/ counting *.rs and matching
  \#\[test\]. No inference. These numbers are the ones to trust.

Signal 2 -- CARD-NUMBER PRESENCE. Per cluster, the set of distinct card_no
  literals in its .rs files is differenced against the set of distinct card_no
  literals in all of engine_c_wip/tests/*.c. Reliable, but only PROBES coverage:
  a card appearing in the C corpus proves the card is *reachable* from some C
  test, not that this cluster's assertions were ported. Used here as a NEGATIVE
  signal only -- a card absent from the whole C corpus is positive proof that no
  C test drives that print.

Signal 3 -- TEST-FUNCTION NAME MATCH. Each Rust \#\[test\] fn name is normalised
  (lowercase, strip a leading test_, drop non-alphanumerics) and compared with
  every C \static void <name>(...)\. This is the WEAKEST signal and it fails in
  BOTH directions, with measured examples:

  FALSE NEGATIVE (a ported test reported as uncovered). Rust
  \debut_recovers_live_card_from_waitroom\ vs C
  \	est_debut_recovers_one_live_card_from_waitroom_to_hand\. The inserted
  "one" breaks the substring, so a test that test_parity_recover_to_hand.c
  genuinely ports is scored uncovered. This is why
  effects/recover/to_hand reads 157/167 uncovered when the C suite has 33
  dedicated test functions for it.

  FALSE POSITIVE (an unported test reported as covered). Rust
  \proof_cost_below_20_no_effect\ matched on a loose containment rule even
  though PL!HS-bp6-029-L appears nowhere in the C corpus outside this survey's
  own probe. The name signal alone would have put effects/look_select/recruit_stage
  at "2 of 4 covered". It is 0 of 4.

  Because of this, the dispatch list in section B requires BOTH signals to fire
  (>=34% of the cluster's card numbers absent AND >=34% of its test names
  unmatched). A cluster that is merely renamed in C stays off the list; a
  cluster that is genuinely untouched is on it.

HEADER COMMENTS ARE NOT TRUSTED. Five C files claim a cluster in their header.
Reading the bodies changed the verdict in five cases:

  1. engine_c_wip/tests/test_move_cards.c:83 cites
     engine/tests/test_modules/effects/conditional/zone_source/
     live_phase_success_zone_replacement_q256_test.rs. It ports ONE arm of ONE
     of that cluster's 10 files. The cluster is 10 files / 59 tests and 5 of its
     distinct card numbers appear nowhere in the C corpus. A header citation is
     a per-test provenance note, NOT a cluster-coverage claim.

  2. engine_c_wip/tests/test_parity_rules.c claims "C port of the
     engine/tests/test_modules/rules/ cluster", but its OWN body at lines
     1359-1379 (test_concession_surface_is_absent,
     test_permanent_loop_action_boundary_is_absent) shows the concession and
     rule-12.1 Rust tests are NOT ported -- they are recorded as C API gaps
     (RB_ACTION_CONCEDE does not exist; GameState::record_action_boundary has
     no counterpart). My survey listed those 13 rules/ tests as uncovered, which
     is the correct answer, but the header would have said otherwise.

  3. engine_c_wip/tests/test_parity_look_reveal.c claims "Parity suite for
     engine/tests/test_modules/effects/look_select/". It does not touch
     look_and_filter (7 cards absent), search_deck (4 absent) or reorder_top
     (4 absent).

  4. engine_c_wip/tests/test_parity_cost_compound.c claims coverage of
     "engine/tests/test_modules/effects/cost_mod". cost_mod/required_hearts has
     5 of 13 card numbers absent (PL!-bp3-021-L, PL!-bp5-020-L, PL!-bp5-023-L,
     PL!-bp6-022-L, PL!-PR-002-PR).

  5. engine_c_wip/tests/test_parity_support.c claims coverage of
     "engine/tests/test_modules/support/". That directory has 4 .rs files and
     ZERO \#\[test] -- it is a helper module, not a test cluster. Any
     "coverage" claim over it is vacuous by construction.

STALENESS. The C corpus grew from 77 to 83 .c files DURING this survey (peers
landed test_parity_jidou_move_yell.c, test_parity_jidou_state.c,
test_parity_jidou_watch.c, test_parity_per_card.c, test_parity_rules_extra.c,
plus this survey's own test_survey_probe.c). The section B dispatch list was
re-verified against the 83-file corpus and was unchanged. Re-run before acting.

================================================================================================================
G. CARD IDENTITY VERIFICATION (AGENTS.md rule) -- Rust fixture bugs found
================================================================================================================

Every card number in the ported probe fixture was checked against
cards/cards.json. All 11 fixtures are PRESENT and their printed costs match
what the Rust test comments claim. One genuine Rust fixture bug was found
elsewhere, in a cluster this survey lists as 0/3 covered:

  engine/tests/test_modules/effects/live_start/dazzling_game_test.rs,
  test dazzling_q187_exclude_selected_liella_other_pickable (lines 158-232).

  Dazzling Game (PL!SP-bp4-023-L, per cards.json) reads:
    "...one member among Kanon, Wien Margarete, Tojo Fuyuri on my stage, AND
     one OTHER 'Liella!' member, gain blade."

  The Rust fixture stages:
    let kanon  = game.id("PL!SP-pb1-001-R"); // comment claims "Liella!"
    let liella = game.id("PL!SP-sd1-002-SD"); // comment claims "Liella!"

  cards/cards.json says:
    PL!SP-pb1-001-R  name=Kan-on / Shibuya Kan-on   unit=CatChu!        cost=11
    PL!SP-sd1-002-SD  name=Tou Kaku (Tang Keke)     unit=KALEIDOSCORE  cost=11

  So BOTH staged members are in the wrong group: neither is Liella!. Kan-on is
  the correct pick for the FIRST selection (she is one of the three named on
  the card), but the SECOND selection -- the one the test exists to pin, the
  Q187 exclude_selected rule -- is driven by a KALEIDOSCORE member. The test
  therefore asserts Q187 against a board where the Q187 clause should not fire
  at all. The in-source comments "Liella!" are wrong for both lines. A correct
  fixture wants a real Liella! member, e.g. PL!SP-pb1-011-R (Tojo Fuyuri,
  Liella!) for the second pick. This is a Rust test bug, not a C port gap, and
  it should be fixed in engine/ before anyone ports the cluster.

  Also confirmed non-ASCII hazard for porters: several fixtures spell card
  numbers with a FULLWIDTH PLUS (U+FF0B), e.g. PL!HS-bp1-004-R+ as
  "PL!HS-bp1-004-R\u{ff0b}". The C port must carry the same byte sequence;
  engine_c_wip/tests/test_survey_probe.c spells it as the ASCII escape
  "\xEF\xBC\x8B" because a PowerShell -Encoding utf8 round trip mangles
  non-ASCII source in this repo.
